title: How Promptly the Cancellation Was Confirmed Bears on an Air Ticket Fare Brands Voucher
content:
A cancellation of an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking confirmed before the aircraft was due to leave leaves more value on the voucher than one confirmed afterwards, but only where the fare brand's credit runs long enough for the distinction to be drawn at all.

## 1. The share carried forward

| Where | The share carried forward is |
| --- | --- |
| the cancellation was confirmed on or before the outbound departure date and the brand's credit runs 12 months or more | 1, the whole of the subtotal |
| the cancellation was confirmed after the outbound departure date and the brand's credit runs 12 months or more | 0.97, being 97 percent |
| in every other case | no such treatment applies to the share |

## 2. The two readings

The date test compares the day the cancellation was confirmed with the outbound departure date: a cancellation confirmed on the departure date itself counts as confirmed on or before it. The brand test reads the credit validity term scheduled for the brand the booking is held in, and is met at 12 months or more.

A booking held in a brand whose credit runs fewer than 12 months falls outside both of the first two rows whenever the cancellation was confirmed.

## 3. Boundary readings, on hypothetical dates

On a booking held in a brand whose credit runs 18 months, a cancellation confirmed on the morning of the outbound departure date is confirmed on that date, so the whole of the subtotal is carried forward. One confirmed the day after the outbound departure date carries 97 percent of it forward.

On a booking held in a brand whose credit runs 0 months, neither of the first two rows can hold, and no such treatment applies however promptly the cancellation was confirmed.
